################################################################################ 

# 0. OVERVIEW & SETUP

################################################################################ 

This script presents [sensitivity analyses]{.underline} with [two-stage meta-regressions]{.underline}, to complement multilevel models with interactions in the main analyses.

For main analyses, see 'Main analyses.Rmd'. For sex-disaggregated analyses, see 'Sex disaggregated.Rmd'.

For other sensitivity analyses, see

- 'Sensitivity analysis - Excluding no denomination.Rmd' for repeat of all analyses excluding no denomination group

- 'Sensitivity analysis - Largest group.Rmd' for repeat of all analyses with the largest group as majority (rather than \>50%)

**Setup**

Load functions, file paths, and packages

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

################################################################################ 

# 1. RANDOM-EFFECTS META-REGRESSIONS

################################################################################ 

In the main analyses we have conducted two-stage meta-analysis, we now add country-level predictors to conduct meta-regressions.

```{r load-data}
country_data <- readRDS("country_data.rds")
country_estimates <- readRDS("country_estimates_ls.rds")
country_estimates_hap <- readRDS("country_estimates_hap.rds")
country_estimates_gh <- readRDS("country_estimates_gh.rds")

# Transform
country_data <- country_data %>%
  mutate(
    gri_category = case_when(
      gri_matched >= 6.6 ~ "Very High",
      gri_matched >= 4.5 ~ "High",
      gri_matched >= 2.4 ~ "Moderate",
      gri_matched >= 0   ~ "Low"          # NA stays NA
    ),
    gri_category = factor(gri_category, levels = c("Low","Moderate","High","Very High")),
    
    shi_category = case_when(
      shi_matched >= 7.2 ~ "Very High",
      shi_matched >= 3.6 ~ "High",
      shi_matched >= 1.5 ~ "Moderate",
      shi_matched >= 0   ~ "Low"          # NA stays NA
    ),
    shi_category = factor(shi_category, levels = c("Low","Moderate","High","Very High")),
    
    log_gdp = log(gdp_matched)
  )

# Merge 
country_estimates <- country_estimates %>%
  left_join(country_data, by = "country")

country_estimates_hap <- country_estimates_hap %>%
  left_join(country_data, by = "country")

country_estimates_gh <- country_estimates_gh %>%
  left_join(country_data, by = "country")

# Check 
names(country_estimates)
```

We want to create a loop that does the meta-regression for each of the country predictors for all 3 outcomes without having to copy and paste many lines of code.

```{r meta-regression-function}

# Create loop
run_meta_regression <- function(data, predictor) {
  
  df <- data %>%
    select(country, estimate, std.error, all_of(predictor)) %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(estimate),
      !is.na(std.error),
      !is.na(.data[[predictor]])
    )
  
  # Null model
  null_model <- rma(
    yi = estimate,
    sei = std.error,
    data = df,
    method = "REML"
  )
  
  # Meta-regression
  meta_reg <- rma(
    yi = estimate,
    sei = std.error,
    mods = as.formula(paste("~", predictor)),
    data = df,
    method = "REML",
    level = 90
  )
  
  # Pseudo R²
  tau2_null  <- null_model$tau2
  tau2_model <- meta_reg$tau2
  
  pseudo_r2 <- if (!is.na(tau2_null) && tau2_null > 0) {
    100 * (tau2_null - tau2_model) / tau2_null
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
  
  pseudo_r2 <- ifelse(pseudo_r2 < 0, 0, pseudo_r2)
  
  coef_table <- as.data.frame(coef(summary(meta_reg)))
  coef_table$term <- rownames(coef_table)
  rownames(coef_table) <- NULL
  
  names(coef_table) <- c("estimate", "se", "zval", "pval", "ci_lb", "ci_ub", "term")
  
  coef_table <- coef_table %>%
    mutate(
      predictor = predictor,
      n_countries = nrow(df),
      QM = meta_reg$QM,
      QM_p = meta_reg$QMp,
      tau2_null = tau2_null,
      tau2_model = tau2_model,
      pseudo_r2 = pseudo_r2
    ) %>%
    select(
      predictor,
      term,
      estimate,
      se,
      ci_lb,
      ci_ub,
      pval,
      n_countries,
      QM,
      QM_p,
      tau2_null,
      tau2_model,
      pseudo_r2
    )
  
    list(
    predictor = predictor,
    n_countries = nrow(df),
    model = meta_reg,
    results = coef_table
  )
  
}
```

Now we review the summary of the random-effects meta-regressions.

```{r meta-regression-summary}
predictors <- c(
  "gri_category",
  "shi_category",
  "democracy_matched",
  "log_gdp",
  "gini_matched"
)

country_estimates <- country_estimates %>%
  mutate(across(c(gri_category, shi_category),
                ~ factor(.x, levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High"))))

meta_regs_ls <- setNames(lapply(predictors, \(x) run_meta_regression(country_estimates, x)), predictors)
meta_regs_hap <- setNames(lapply(predictors, \(x) run_meta_regression(country_estimates_hap, x)), predictors)
meta_regs_gh <- setNames(lapply(predictors, \(x) run_meta_regression(country_estimates_gh, x)), predictors)

meta_reg_ls_table <- bind_rows(lapply(meta_regs_ls, \(x) x$results)) %>%
  mutate(outcome = "Life satisfaction", .before = 1)

meta_reg_hap_table <- bind_rows(lapply(meta_regs_hap, \(x) x$results)) %>%
  mutate(outcome = "Happiness", .before = 1)

meta_reg_gh_table <- bind_rows(lapply(meta_regs_gh, \(x) x$results)) %>%
  mutate(outcome = "General health", .before = 1)

meta_reg_results <- bind_rows(meta_reg_ls_table, meta_reg_hap_table, meta_reg_gh_table)
meta_reg_results
```

Although not reported, we want to visualise the plots and compare to the mixed-effects models previously completed.

```{r meta-regression-plots}
plot_meta_regression <- function(meta_reg_obj, predictor, outcome_label, data) {
  
  # For categorical predictors
  if (predictor %in% c("gri_category", "shi_category")) {
    
    # Get fitted values per category
    pred_df <- data %>%
      filter(!is.na(.data[[predictor]]), !is.na(estimate), !is.na(std.error)) %>%
      mutate(category = .data[[predictor]],
             precision = 1 / std.error^2)
    
    # Get meta-regression predictions per category
    fit <- meta_reg_obj$model
    pred_levels <- levels(pred_df$category)
    
    ggplot(pred_df, aes(x = category, y = estimate)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
      geom_point(aes(size = precision), colour = "#0B2A5B", alpha = 0.4) +
      stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "point", 
                   size = 4, shape = 18, colour = "#04BFAF") +
      scale_size_continuous(name = "Precision (1/SE²)", range = c(1, 8)) +
      labs(
        x = ifelse(predictor == "gri_category", 
                   "Government Restrictions Index (GRI)",
                   "Social Hostilities Index (SHI)"),
        y = "Country-level minority-majority gap estimate",
        title = paste(outcome_label, "— meta-regression:", 
                      ifelse(predictor == "gri_category", "GRI", "SHI"))
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
    
  } else {
    
    # For continuous predictors — bubble plot
    pred_df <- data %>%
      filter(!is.na(.data[[predictor]]), !is.na(estimate), !is.na(std.error)) %>%
      mutate(precision = 1 / std.error^2)
    
    # Get regression line from model
    x_seq <- seq(min(pred_df[[predictor]], na.rm = TRUE),
                 max(pred_df[[predictor]], na.rm = TRUE),
                 length.out = 100)
    
    # Predicted values from meta-regression
    new_data <- data.frame(x_seq)
    names(new_data) <- predictor
    pred_line <- predict(meta_reg_obj$model, newmods = x_seq)
    
    line_df <- data.frame(
      x = x_seq,
      pred = pred_line$pred,
      ci_lb = pred_line$ci.lb,
      ci_ub = pred_line$ci.ub
    )
    
    x_label <- case_when(
      predictor == "log_gdp"          ~ "Log GDP per capita",
      predictor == "democracy_matched" ~ "Democracy Index",
      predictor == "gini_matched"      ~ "Gini Index",
      TRUE ~ predictor
    )
    
    ggplot() +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
      geom_ribbon(data = line_df,
                  aes(x = x, ymin = ci_lb, ymax = ci_ub),
                  alpha = 0.15, fill = "#04BFAF") +
      geom_line(data = line_df,
                aes(x = x, y = pred),
                colour = "#04BFAF", linewidth = 1) +
      geom_point(data = pred_df,
                 aes(x = .data[[predictor]], y = estimate, size = precision),
                 colour = "#0B2A5B", alpha = 0.5) +
      geom_text_repel(data = pred_df,
                      aes(x = .data[[predictor]], y = estimate, label = country),
                      size = 3, max.overlaps = 10) +
      scale_size_continuous(name = "Precision (1/SE²)", range = c(1, 8)) +
      labs(
        x = x_label,
        y = "Country-level minority-majority gap estimate",
        title = paste(outcome_label, "— meta-regression:", x_label)
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  }
}

# Generate plots for life satisfaction
for (pred in predictors) {
  p <- plot_meta_regression(meta_regs_ls[[pred]], pred, "Life satisfaction", country_estimates)
  print(p)
}

# Generate plots for happiness
for (pred in predictors) {
  p <- plot_meta_regression(meta_regs_hap[[pred]], pred, "Happiness", country_estimates_hap)
  print(p)
}

# Generate plots for general health
for (pred in predictors) {
  p <- plot_meta_regression(meta_regs_gh[[pred]], pred, "General health", country_estimates_gh)
  print(p)
}
```

Now this has all worked well, but for religious minority group size we can't easily run meta-regressions because there isn't a single value for each country of religious minority group size like the other country-level indices. We will keep only results from multi-level models and not run meta-regressions.
